findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "password_generate" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "http_status_code" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: email_security_check, website_health_check, http_headers_check, seo_page_check, sitemap_validate, email_address_validate · Private data: dns_lookup, noise_exposure, password_generate, jwt_decode, subnet_calculator, mime_type_lookup, dns_propagation, email_address_validate · Public sink: email_security_check, website_health_check, subnet_calculator, email_address_validate · Destructive: website_health_check, json_format_validate, cron_explain, arabic_numbers_convert.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: email_security_check, website_health_check, http_headers_check, seo_page_check, sitemap_validate, email_address_validate · Private data: dns_lookup, noise_exposure, password_generate, jwt_decode, subnet_calculator, mime_type_lookup, dns_propagation, email_address_validate · Public sink: email_security_check, website_health_check, subnet_calculator, email_address_validate · Destructive: website_health_check, json_format_validate, cron_explain, arabic_numbers_convert

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
